prompt:
Grace just briefed me on the external security audit findings. It's worse than I expected. They flagged us on access controls: over-scoped permissions, credential red flags, and basically no process for locking people out when they leave or change roles. She wants a full picture of every security or access incident from the past 90 days before she and Denise sit down with Robert for the quarterly review.

I know bits and pieces. Keisha had some kind of credential issue a few weeks back, there was a situation with an intern accessing borrower records he had no business looking at, and Marcus Webb's exit was not clean from an IT standpoint. But I'm only in the office two days a week, so I'm sure I'm missing things that were discussed in channels I don't monitor closely. Grace also mentioned Victor flagged some payment activity that doesn't track, which could tie into the same governance issues. I need to understand what he actually found and whether there's an access or financial exposure tied to it.

For everything you turn up, I need the actual scope: which borrower records or loans were directly at risk in each case, whether each gap has been closed or is still open, and if there are any accounts on our systems right now that shouldn't be. Reconcile the current staff roster against what you can find for recent activity across our platforms. Then send Grace and Denise a single briefing covering each incident with the exposure details and a prioritized list of what needs to be locked down first. Drop a summary in the compliance channel as well so there's a formal record, and make sure any loans you can tie to an incident get flagged with notes about it.

criteria.criterion: The Agent sends the security/access incident briefing email to [grace.yamamoto@keystonemortgage.com](mailto:grace.yamamoto@keystonemortgage.com) and [denise.holloway@keystonemortgage.com](mailto:denise.holloway@keystonemortgage.com).
criteria.evidence: Look for a send_email call whose recipients include grace.yamamoto@keystonemortgage.com and denise.holloway@keystonemortgage.com (OE 16).
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt's primary write action is 'send Grace and Denise a single briefing.' Both recipients are set in the same email, so they are checked together.

criteria.evidence: send_email content covers Keisha's portal compromise and the exposure of borrower loan files (OE 7).
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks the briefing to cover the compromised-portal incident and its exposure. The specific loans are independently enforced by the per-loan flag rubrics, so this stays a single atomic incident-exposure claim.

criteria.evidence: send_email content covers the spoofed-wire fraud on LN-2026-00605 / Destiny Pham (OE 12).
criteria.cb_justification: A security incident in the window that the prompt scopes in; verifier runs confirm it is achievable (covered in Run 3). The loan number identifies the single wire-fraud incident (one finding).

criteria.criterion: The Agent covers a payment-governance anomaly flagged by Victor Osei in the briefing email to Grace Yamamoto and Denise Holloway at least one of: the unsupported recurring Premier Data Solutions payments, the DeLuca Appraisal Group appraisal-steering payments, or the ongoing commission payments to departed loan officer Marcus Webb.
criteria.evidence: send_email content covers at least one payment-governance anomaly tied to Victor Osei (Premier Data Solutions / DeLuca appraisal steering / departed-LO commissions) (OE 13).
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks the agent to understand what Victor flagged and its exposure. Victor's flag maps to more than one payment anomaly in the universe, so accepting any one avoids failing a valid alternative path (verifier runs showed agents reasonably picked different ones DeLuca, departed-LO commissions, or Premier Data).

criteria.criterion: The Agent distinguishes which incident gaps are already closed versus still open in the briefing email to Grace Yamamoto and Denise Holloway (for example, Evan Mercer's LOS access disabled = closed, while Marcus Webb's credential revocation is unconfirmed and/or Keisha's credential-reuse exposure remains open) (or similar).
criteria.evidence: send_email content indicates open-vs-closed status across the incidents (OEs 7-13).
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt explicitly asks 'whether each gap has been closed or is still open.' Phrased flexibly since the exact wording is free-text.

criteria.criterion: The Agent includes a prioritized list of what to lock down first, drawn from the still-open gaps, in the briefing email to Grace Yamamoto and Denise Holloway (or similar).
criteria.evidence: send_email content contains a prioritized lockdown list (OE 16).
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks for 'a prioritized list of what needs to be locked down first.' The specific ordering is agent judgment, so this is flexible.
